mathematical_premises: Target inputs have an absolutely continuous product law because each physical marginal has a density.
A target matrix is nonzero and in fact has rank at least three.
Coarea away from the critical affine subspace proves absolute continuity of any nonconstant quadratic pushforward.
Lebesgue differentiation for one-dimensional L1 densities recovers density values at almost every point from a fixed compact approximate identity after scaling the matrix.
Original-coordinate bathtub optimization is valid separately in each physical marginal for the positive bounded kernel payoff.
new_results: For every nonnegative compactly supported L1 kernel K of mass one and every R>0, the sharp QFORM constant C_* equals sup_{target, |y|>=R} s_3(A) E K(y-X^TAX), in the extended sense, without assuming continuity or boundedness of the individual raw density.

For one fixed C-infinity bump kappa supported in (-1,1), the full target is exactly equivalent to a positive fixed-scale smooth integral with |y|>=2, hence separated from the only critical output value zero.

The same sharp supremum can be restricted to original-coordinate indicator marginals 1_{E_i}, |E_i|=1, and then to bounded finite unions of intervals, with no uniform fragment-count or separation bound.
The smoothed profile H(y)=E kappa(y-Q) has uniform derivative bounds ||H^(m)||_infinity<=||kappa^(m)||_infinity for every m; this is distinct from raw-output regularity.

partner_result_applied.statement: A definite original-coordinate 2x2 principal block B gives ||p_Q||_infinity<=pi/sqrt(|det B|) under arbitrary outside couplings.
partner_result_applied.application: s_3(A) E kappa(y-Q)<=pi s_3(A)/sqrt(|det B|); if |det B|>=eta s_3(A)^2 this is <=pi/sqrt(eta).
